about: Starter swaps: parts a person swaps into any toolkit's cart, each a published row (type record:toolkit-swap) whose `swap` is handed in as toolkit_choice.swap, so a way of setting up is chosen apart from the work a toolkit does: any toolkit with any swap is a cart, and no toolkit is written once per way. A pointer is the same { id, door, speaks, label?, credential? } a toolkit's stack holds (read-data/stack-policy.json); a credential is the NAME a person keeps the key under in their vault, never the key. Each part named here is a tool the Workshop ships. The starter toolkits already host on a computer of the person's own (rented, or one they run); these swaps cover a site on the person's own domain with their own sign-in, and a Linux machine the person already runs taken first. A site with no domain of its own has no swap: the names it would get under a shared address were given by the forwarder, which the engine dropped on Nov 15 2026 (trillion-rust f450c37a4), and no computer runs it now, so tool:name_site and tool:attach_domain cannot run (each answers no_host_actions). An agency runs the own-domain swap once per client, each its own cart; a person on a phone alone takes the toolkit as it stands, whose sign-in already offers passkeys. A company's own sign-in (OIDC or SAML through its identity provider) has no part yet: the official Better Auth tool runs no single sign-on plugin, so no swap offers it.

payload.title: My own domain and my own sign-in
payload.description: Your own domain points at your computer, and your computer runs your own sign-in.

payload.title: A Linux machine I already run
payload.description: The machine you already have is set up over SSH, and every program is built there from its public source.
